question: Who does Lencho have complete faith in? Which sentences in the story tell you this?
answer:
Lencho has complete faith in God. He believes that God knows everything and always helps those who are in trouble. This faith is reflected in several sentences from the story:

• 'But in the hearts of all who lived in that solitary house in the middle of the valley, there was a single hope: help from God.'
• 'All through the night, Lencho thought only of his one hope: the help of God, whose eyes, as he had been instructed, see everything, even what is deep in one's conscience.'
• 'God,' he wrote, 'if you don't help me, my family and I will go hungry this year.'
• He wrote 'To God' on the envelope and posted the letter.
• 'God could not have made a mistake, nor could he have denied Lencho what he had requested.'

question: Why does the postmaster send money to Lencho? Why does he sign the letter 'God'?
answer: The postmaster is deeply moved by Lencho's unwavering faith in God. He does not want that faith to be shaken, so he collects money from his colleagues and contributes part of his own salary. He signs the letter 'God' so that Lencho continues to believe that God has answered his prayer.

question: Did Lencho try to find out who had sent the money to him? Why or why not?
answer: No, Lencho never tried to discover who had actually sent the money. His faith in God was so strong that he believed without any doubt that the money had come directly from God. He could not imagine that ordinary people would help him.

question: Who does Lencho think has taken the rest of the money? What is the irony in the situation?
answer: Lencho believes that the post office employees have stolen the remaining thirty pesos because he had asked God for one hundred pesos but received only seventy. The irony is that the same post office employees who generously collected money to help him are accused of being 'a bunch of crooks' by the very person they were trying to help.

question: Are there people like Lencho in the real world? What kind of a person would you say he is?
answer: People with such absolute and unquestioning faith are rare in the modern world. Lencho is best described as naive, unquestioning, honest and deeply faithful. Although he wrongly suspects the post office employees, his actions arise from his complete belief in God rather than from selfishness or greed.

question: There are two kinds of conflict in the story—between humans and nature and between humans themselves. How are these conflicts illustrated?
answer: The conflict between humans and nature is shown when the hailstorm destroys Lencho's entire crop despite months of hard work, leaving his family without food or income. The conflict between humans themselves appears when Lencho wrongly accuses the kind-hearted post office employees of stealing the missing money. Although they helped him selflessly, he loses faith in people while keeping complete faith in God.
